title: Cost-tiered spillplan and accelerator affinity policy for cross-region routing
creator: Priya Sharma
description:
Problem: We need a routing policy that jointly respects per-customer budget caps and accelerator economics while keeping latency SLOs. Current region-tier routing either prefers cheapest endpoints (risking spot eviction) or strictly enforces latency-first routing (higher cost). This ticket designs and implements a ‘soft spill’ plan combined with an accelerator affinity score so requests can be moved across regions and GPU classes incrementally when budget headroom is low, without large latency regressions or QoS failures.

Goals:
- Enforce per-customer daily/weekly budget caps at request-routing time (soft throttles + hard cutover)
- Prefer lower-cost accelerator types (spot, older GPU classes) but back off gracefully on evictions or latency degradation
- Provide deterministic, observable fallback to on-demand GPUs or cheaper model variants when budget headroom exhausted
- Produce telemetry for cost-per-token, tail latency, and eviction exposure per customer/route

Design (high level):
1) Accelerator Affinity Score: compute a score for each candidate endpoint combining normalized price-per-token, estimated p99 latency delta, and eviction-risk factor. Score = w_cost*(price_rank) + w_latency*(latency_rank) + w_eviction*(eviction_risk). Weights are tunable per-customer tier.
2) Soft Spill Plan: when an endpoint's projected spend for a customer approaches the configured soft cap (e.g., 80% of daily limit), start progressive spillover: 10% of traffic moves to the next-best cheaper region/GPU every minute, capped by a per-route spill window. If soft cap triggers while in-progress, escalate to hard fallback (route to on-demand or lower-cost model variant).
3) Budget Guardrails: implement two enforcement modes: soft (probabilistic spill + sampling for latency tests) and hard (reject/queue or route to degraded model). Admins can configure per-customer preference (latency-priority | cost-priority | balanced).
4) Fallback Model Variants: when accelerator capacity is limited or cost caps reached, automatically select pre-validated cheaper model variants (quantized or smaller family) with a quality-loss budget. The policy must store mapping: original_model -> [variant_a, variant_b] with expected quality deltas.
5) Telemetry & Alerts: expose metrics per-customer: spend_rate, percent_spilled, spill_latency_delta, eviction_rate, fallback_rate. Create dashboard and alert if fallback_rate > X% or spill_latency_delta > 50ms for 5m.

Implementation notes:
- Routing decision lives inside the router service (router-service v2). Implement a pluggable PolicyEvaluator that scores candidates and returns ordered endpoints plus spill instructions.
- Persist per-customer spending cursors in Redis with 1s resolution and backs up to billing DB every 30s for reconciliation.
- Use probabilistic sampling (1%) to send mirrored traffic to candidate endpoints for latency and output-quality checks before full spillover.
- Integrate with existing spot-eviction detector: if eviction risk spikes, affinity score sharply increases eviction penalty to avoid placing traffic.

Rollout plan:
- Phase A (Canary): implement policy evaluator behind feature flag for 5 internal customers in us-west-2, limited to 1% traffic. Monitor cost-per-token and p99.
- Phase B (Gradual): increase to 10 customers and 10% traffic, tune weights and soft cap thresholds.
- Phase C (Full): enable per-customer config UI in Console and allow opt-in to cost-priority mode.

Acceptance criteria:
- Router can compute affinity scores and execute soft spill without manual intervention.
- No customer experiences >3x increase in tail latency during spill operations in canary.
- Billing reconciliation shows routing decisions respect configured caps within 0.5% error.

Risks & mitigations:
- Incorrect spend estimates causing premature hard cutovers: mitigate by conservative initial thresholds and realtime reconciliation.
- Quality regressions when routing to model variants: maintain per-customer evals and automatic rollback triggers.
- Region-wide spot evictions causing correlated fallbacks: add cross-region headroom hedging to avoid cascading cost spikes.

Deliverables:
- router-service: PolicyEvaluator implementation + feature flag
- runtime: lightweight telemetry hooks for spill decisions
- console: per-customer budget config and visibility (read-only at Canary)
- dashboards and alerts: Grafana + PagerDuty rule

Links: [PRD internal doc] https://confluence.redwood.ai/prd/smart-routing-spillplan, [Design notes] https://docs.redwood.ai/design/accelerator-affinity, [Spike PR] https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/1298
